flow_intro: Select a stage in the loop to see its cash flows, control points, and exposure.

flow.heading: Household savings
flow.description: Households are the starting point for retirement capital and the endpoint for both investment outcomes and changes in earned income. These exposures do not necessarily offset each other.
items: Contributions from earned income enter retirement arrangements.
Savings are allocated through pension institutions and investment mandates.
Beneficiaries may receive investment gains through the rules of their retirement plan.
Households face investment uncertainty and wage risk, with different timing and distribution.

flow.heading: Public pensions
flow.description: Pension institutions invest on behalf of beneficiaries. Their mandates, liquidity needs, and manager choices shape which assets retirement capital can reach.
items: Contributions and portfolio cash flows support the investment pool.
Capital is committed to managers or invested in assets; commitments are not the same as cash deployed.
Beneficiaries have claims defined by plan rules; investment managers may earn fees.
Portfolio losses, illiquidity, and funding pressures affect institutions and their stakeholders.

flow.heading: VC / PE funds
flow.description: Fund managers connect institutional capital with private companies. Access to deals, investment terms, and ownership stakes determine how returns are shared.
items: Limited partners commit capital under fund agreements.
Funds invest in companies and may make follow-on investments.
Managers may earn management fees and carried interest; investors receive distributions under the contract.
Investors carry company and liquidity risk; fees and financing terms affect net returns.

flow.heading: AI companies
flow.description: Funding expands capacity, but raising capital is not the same as generating revenue or profit. Customers still need to pay for reliable results.
items: Equity or debt finances development and operations; customer revenue is a separate flow.
Companies pay for compute, staff, data, distribution, and integration.
Owners retain residual returns when revenue exceeds costs; customers may capture savings through lower prices.
Investors face business risk, customers face delivery risk, and workers face changing tasks and pay.

flow.heading: Compute & energy
flow.description: AI spending creates demand for infrastructure. Scarce capacity can strengthen a supplier’s bargaining position, but expansion costs and competing supply can erode returns.
items: Cloud contracts, equipment purchases, and infrastructure finance support capacity.
Providers fund equipment, construction, electricity, operations, and financing.
Suppliers and asset owners may capture margins, interest, or infrastructure cash flows.
Owners face utilization, construction, financing, and obsolescence risk; energy costs can affect other users.

flow.heading: Jobs repriced
flow.description: Changes in tasks and organizations affect wages and employment. The buyout snapshot illustrates organizational change; it does not prove that AI replaced the eligible roles.
items: Workers receive wages; eligible households may also receive investment benefits.
Households spend, save, and contribute to retirement arrangements.
Productivity gains may accrue to employers, customers, or workers depending on competition and bargaining.
Workers may face displacement or retraining costs; investment ownership does not guarantee compensation.

region_notes.US: An intermediary route: pension institutions select private-market managers. Net beneficiary returns depend on underlying holdings, fees, investment terms, and benefit rules. Private VC exposure does not capture listed AI holdings.
region_notes.Canada: Ownership and lending create different claims. A data-center stake offers residual ownership returns; a loan offers contractual interest and repayment rights. Neither is equivalent to owning a model company.
region_notes.UK: The private-markets target is broader than the current unlisted-equity measure. Keep policy pledges, binding commitments, capital calls, and invested assets separate when assessing progress.
region_notes.EU: The comparison mixes a pension-and-insurance asset stock with venture commitments over a decade. It is not a current AI portfolio weight, and low domestic VC commitments do not establish an absence of global AI exposure.
region_notes.Japan: The alternatives share and allocation cap describe capacity, not promised AI spending. A direct commitment to a private-equity fund is also different from directly owning its portfolio companies.
region_notes.Singapore: Sovereign investors can hold claims across the AI stack. Sovereign assets are distinct from personal pension accounts; how returns reach households depends on institutional and fiscal arrangements.

mechanism_heading: What turns a bottleneck into returns

mechanisms.title: Reliable results
mechanisms.body: Technical capacity creates an opportunity only when a result meets the required quality, timing, and responsibility standard. More calls do not automatically mean more useful output.

mechanisms.title: Paying demand
mechanisms.body: Customers need budgets and a reason to pay. Lower delivery costs may increase volume, but competition can pass those savings to customers rather than company owners.

mechanisms.title: Control and ownership
mechanisms.body: Customer relationships, scarce resources, switching costs, and contracts influence bargaining power. Ownership and financing then determine who has a claim on the cash flows.

model_note: The model distinguishes value creation from value capture: solving a constraint can benefit customers or society without giving the solver lasting pricing power.

glossary.title: Capital flow is not a complete accounting loop
glossary.body: The arrows illustrate a mechanism, not matching transactions or a measured causal chain. Wages, public markets, taxes, and other financing routes also matter.

glossary.title: Commitment is not deployment
glossary.body: A pledge states an intention. A binding fund commitment creates an obligation. A capital call transfers cash. Asset value measures holdings at a point in time. Realized distributions return cash to investors.

glossary.title: Ownership is not an automatic hedge
glossary.body: A household’s labor income and investment returns can move differently. Coverage, benefit rules, fees, timing, and the distribution of gains determine whether investment exposure cushions wage losses.

glossary.title: Evidence has limits
glossary.body: A source link records provenance, not independent verification. Pending links remain pending. Dates, geography, asset classes, and denominators must match before percentages can be compared.
